Caterpillar (forest) plot of the site effects

Source: R/plot-sites.R
plot_sites.Rd

plot_sites() makes a caterpillar plot, or forest plot, of the site effects. Each row is a labeled site with the posterior mean of its effect, an outer and an inner posterior interval, and its estimate. When there are many sites, the plot can be limited to selected sites or to the sites with the lowest and the highest posterior means.

Usage

plot_sites(
  x,
  sites = NULL,
  n_extreme = NULL,
  sort_by = c("mean", "sigma", "observed", "prob", "none"),
  level = 0.9,
  inner_level = 0.5,
  highlight = NULL,
  show_observed = TRUE,
  ref = c("mean_g", "zero", "none"),
  truth = NULL,
  max_sites = 100,
  scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

sites

Sites to plot, specified as a numeric vector of positions in the data or a character vector of site labels. If NULL (the default), all sites are plotted.

n_extreme

An optional integer. If specified, only the n_extreme sites with the lowest and the n_extreme sites with the highest posterior means are plotted, in two panels. Cannot be used together with sites.

sort_by

Variable by which the sites are ordered: "mean" (the default) for the posterior mean, "sigma" for the standard error, "observed" for the estimate, or "prob" for the probability that the effect is positive. "none" keeps the order of the data.

level

Posterior probability of the outer interval, a number between 0 and 1.

inner_level

Posterior probability of the inner interval, a number between 0 and level. The inner interval is shown as a thicker line. Use NULL to omit it.

highlight

Sites to show in a different color, specified in the same way as sites. If NULL (the default), no site is highlighted.

show_observed

If TRUE (the default), the estimates are shown as open circles.

ref

Where to place the dashed reference line: at the posterior mean of the mean of \(g\) ("mean_g", the default) or at zero ("zero"). Use "none" for no line.

truth

An optional numeric vector with the true effect of every site, for simulated data. The true effects are shown as crosses.

max_sites

Maximum number of sites that are plotted with labels. See Details for how a larger number of sites is shown.

scale

Positive number by which the effects are multiplied in the plot, e.g., scale = 100 to show differences in proportions as percentage points.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The point in each row is the posterior mean, the thick line is the inner interval and the thin line is the outer interval. The open circle is the estimate, so its distance from the point is the shrinkage of the site, i.e., how far the model moves the estimate (plot_shrinkage() shows this for all sites together). The dashed line is the reference line selected with ref.

The plot shows the values returned by site_summary(), so its intervals are the intervals of confint.bef_fit_re() at the same level.

If more than max_sites sites are to be plotted, they are shown as thin lines without labels, inner intervals or estimates, and a message explains how to select fewer sites.

See also

site_summary(), plot_shrinkage(), plot_exceedance(), vignette("plots")

Examples

# The 10 firms with the smallest and the 10 with the largest gaps, in
# percentage points.
plot_sites(krw_fit, n_extreme = 10, scale = 100)


# All 19 studies, ordered by standard error.
plot_sites(raudenbush_fit, sort_by = "sigma", ref = "zero")


# 1,500 sites: lines without labels.
plot_sites(twin_towers_fit)
#> There are 1500 sites to draw, more than `max_sites` (100), so they are drawn without labels. Choose fewer with `sites` or `n_extreme`, or raise `max_sites`.
